extractedItems.title: Moving or bending grass before your shot
extractedItems.question: You find your ball in tall grass. Are you allowed to move or bend the grass if it makes your shot easier?

choices.text: Yes, you can move or bend the grass to help your shot.
No, you must play the ball as it lies and not move the grass.
Yes, but only if you tell your playing partners first.

extractedItems.explanation: You must accept the lie as you find it and are not allowed to move, bend, or break anything growing or fixed to help your shot. Doing so means two penalty strokes.

extractedItems.title: Penalty for breaking off branches during a practice swing
extractedItems.question: You make a practice swing and snap a small branch, which gives you an easier shot. What is the penalty?

choices.text: No penalty.
1 penalty stroke.
2 penalty strokes.
You must replay the shot.

extractedItems.explanation: If you break or bend something during a practice swing that improves your shot, it is two penalty strokes.

extractedItems.title: Playing out of turn to save time
extractedItems.question: You and your friends agree to play out of turn to speed up play. Is there a penalty if no one gets a special advantage?

choices.text: Yes, everyone gets a penalty.
No penalty as long as it’s just to save time.
Only the first player receives a penalty.

extractedItems.explanation: No penalty if playing out of turn is just to save time and not to give anyone a tactical advantage.

choices.text: No penalty as long as they both agree.

extractedItems.explanation: If players agree to play out of order to give an advantage, each gets two penalty strokes.
